newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle, feeder cattle end higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle, feeder cattle end higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher, with much of the late buying in live cattle attributed to shortcovering after the steep break Wednesday, floor sources said.
Buying in feeder cattle began in earnest late after live cattle extended gains.

In live cattle, meat packers buying back short positions appeared to the primary supporting factor. Packers hedged purchases of contract cattle some time ago and after taking delivery of them this week bought back the short positions, they said.

Traders said cash fundamentals remain bearish with lower cash cattle prices expected next week and lower cash beef prices at midday Thursday. They said meat packers may drop cattle bids to $66.00 to $67.00 per cwt next week from $68.00 trades this week.
In feeder cattle, higher cash prices this week coupled with sagging corn prices fueled buying.
Refco led buying of March feeders while RB&H bought May, sources said.
The latest CME cash feeder cattle index released Wednesday was down 0.04 cent at 64.96 cents per lb, but this followed gains Monday and Tuesady of 0.73 and 0.56 cent, respectively.
Live cattle closed up 0.675 to 0.150 cent, with December up 0.525 at 66.425 cents a lb. Feeders finished up 0.500 to 0.200 cent, with January up 0.475 at 66.950.
